headline: Should You Keep Your Tub or Convert to a Walk-In Shower?
articleBody:
Deciding whether to keep an existing bathtub or convert it into a walk-in shower is one of the most common dilemmas in small bathroom design. Both options offer practical advantages depending on your household dynamics and routines.

How to Compare Your Options
Converting to a walk-in shower creates an open, modern atmosphere in compact spaces. Removing a bulky tub apron expands floor sightlines, simplifies daily entry, and provides clean accessibility. Shower conversions also allow for customized wall tile, built-in niches, and clear glass doors that make narrow rooms feel significantly wider.

Keeping a standard tub-and-shower combination makes sense if you have young children, rely on bathing pets, or own a home where this is the sole bathtub on the property. Preserving the tub maintains standard multi-generational utility without requiring adjustments to existing plumbing drain footprints.

What Can Change the Right Choice
Your home’s overall layout plays a major role. If another bathroom in the house already features a full-sized tub, converting the smaller secondary or primary bath to a shower is usually a safe choice that improves daily convenience. If you decide to convert, moving the drain or reconfiguring water lines often requires licensed plumbing work and local permits.
